newsitem.title: USA: Aetna says layoffs 25 pct completed in '96.
newsitem.headline: Aetna says layoffs 25 pct completed in '96.

text.p: Slightly more than 25 percent of the planned 9,373 job cuts announced by Aetna Inc last year were completed by the end of 1996, Aetna said in its annual report.
The rest of the layoffs will occur this year and next, the health insurance and financial services company said.

Most of the job cuts are the result of restructuring announced last year. Aetna sold its property-casualty insurance business to Travelers Group Inc for $4.1 billion in April 1996, and last July announced an $8.9 billion acquisition and merger with U.S. Healthcare.
Aetna employed 30,850 people at the end of 1996, company spokesman Fred Laberge said. It had 9,734 employees in Connecticut at the end of last year.
Aetna said it cut 2,421 jobs last year.

Laberge emphasized that not all of the jobs cut by Aetna left Connecticut. Some 350 former Aetna print shop employees, for example, were taken on by a new employer when Aetna sold its print business to Toronto-based Moore Corp last year, Laberge said.

"The net number of job losses is expected to be about 4,400," Laberge said, referring to the total number of job cuts resulting from the restructuring. "We anticipate hiring people as we consolidate in some areas."
After last year's restructuring, the company is now focused in three main areas: Aetna U.S. Healthcare, Aetna Retirement Services and International.

The company said in its annual report it expected Aetna U.S. Healthcare to be the company's main source of earnings. It plans to enter new geographic markets and expand its presence in the Medicare and commercial risk business.
Aetna said it may seek investments or divestitures in order to accomplish those goals.
